walkthroughs.body_html:
Your body has two ways to send messages.

Nervous system: electrical signals along neurones — fast, short-lived, very precise targets.

Endocrine system: chemical hormones in the blood — slower, longer-lasting, broader effects.

The pituitary in the brain is the master gland — it controls many others by releasing its own hormones.

The thyroid releases thyroxine (metabolism). The pancreas releases insulin and glucagon. The adrenals release adrenaline.

The ovaries in females release oestrogen.

The testes in males release testosterone.

These trigger puberty changes and control fertility — hormones reach every cell via the blood, so effects can be body-wide.

Faster and longer
Identical in speed

options: Thyroid
Pancreas
Pituitary

mcqs.q: How do hormones reach their target organs?
options: They are carried in the bloodstream and act on cells with specific receptors for that hormone.
Reflexes are faster because they use specially fast neurones not used elsewhere.
Hormones are sent through nerves directly to specific organs.
Hormones are released directly into target organs by being injected by glands.

mcqs.q: What does insulin do to blood glucose?
options: Reflexes are faster because they use specially fast neurones not used elsewhere.
It lowers blood glucose by causing cells (especially liver and muscle) to take it up and store it as glycogen.
Insulin destroys glucose in the bloodstream so it cannot be used.
Insulin raises blood glucose to give the body energy.

mcqs.q: Why is a reflex action faster than a conscious response?
options: The brain decides reflexes faster than other actions because it skips thinking.
The signal does not need to be processed by the brain — it travels through a simpler reflex arc via the spinal cord.
Reflexes are faster because they use specially fast neurones not used elsewhere.
Insulin destroys glucose in the bloodstream so it cannot be used.
